app.readerText: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife. However little known the feelings or views of such a man may be on his first entering a neighbourhood, this truth is so well fixed in the minds of the surrounding families, that he is considered as the rightful property of some one or other of their daughters.

mission.text: We believe humanity's literary heritage should not be behind a paywall. At Scrollia there are no walls: anyone can read it, in any language.
mission.quote: “A good book is the precious life-blood of a master spirit, embalmed and treasured up on purpose to a life beyond life.”

privacy.description: Privacy policy for Scrollia and Scrollia for Android.
privacy.caption: Privacy
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.meta: Scrollia and Scrollia for Android · Effective October 27, 2026
privacy.summary: Scrollia has no accounts, ads, or advertising analytics. We do not sell data or build reader profiles. Your library, reading progress, and settings stay on your device. The app and website use HTTPS to contact api.scrollia.org for catalog data and downloads.
privacy.controller: This policy covers Scrollia, its website, and its Android app. For privacy questions or requests, email contact@scrollia.org.
privacy.device: Downloaded or imported books, reading progress, and preferences are stored locally. Scrollia does not sync them to an account or send them to our servers. Imports use Android's file picker; we do not request broad storage, contacts, location, camera, or microphone access. Android automatic backup is disabled for the app.
privacy.logs1: Browsing the catalog, searching, loading a cover, or downloading a book sends a request to our server. Standard technical logs may include the time, IP address, user agent, and requested URL; a search URL may contain your search term. We use these records only to operate, secure, and troubleshoot the service, not for advertising or profiling.
privacy.logs2: Records remain in the server journal until automatic rotation under the system's storage limits. We do not expose your search history to other users. You may request information or deletion through the contact above; identifying specific historical entries may be necessary and requests may be subject to technical or legal obligations.
privacy.providers1: Cloudflare delivers and protects connections to scrollia.org and api.scrollia.org and processes connection data such as IP addresses under its own privacy policy. We include no advertising or analytics SDKs.
privacy.providers2: Google Translate receives selected text only when you choose Translate and the browser opens. We do not send text to Google automatically. That use is governed by Google's policy.
privacy.content: Summaries come from Wikipedia and are attributed under CC BY-SA 4.0. Fonts ship with the app or website; they are not loaded from Google Fonts or other third-party font services.
privacy.deletion: You can remove books in the app. Uninstalling deletes its local library, progress, and settings; original files you imported are not modified. There is no Scrollia account to delete. Connections to our services use HTTPS.
privacy.children: Scrollia is a general-audience library and is not specifically directed at children under 13. We do not request age or school data. Cloudflare may process connections in other countries; this policy applies regardless of your location.
privacy.changes: We will publish any changes here with a new effective date. The policy is not changed through the app without a version you can read on this page.

faq.description: Frequently asked questions about Scrollia: translations, rights, and languages.
faq.caption: Help
faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Short answers about the public domain, translations, copyright, and languages. If yours is missing, email contact@scrollia.org.
faq.aiTitle: Why are there AI translations when others already exist?
faq.ai: We only translate with AI when there is no digitized public-domain historical translation, or when an existing one is still under copyright in many countries. For example, for Alice, Gutiérrez Gili’s Spanish version (1927) is not digitized anywhere, and Lobato’s Portuguese version is still protected in the U.S. AI prepares a draft; then comes editorial and human review. That translation is CC0 (you may copy and improve it without asking), it is always noted in the colophon, and when a free historical edition appears we offer that too.
faq.langTitle: Why don’t I see book X in my language?
faq.lang: Editions in each language are added gradually: first we need a free source or a reviewed translation. We could dump a whole book through an automatic translator (for example Google), but for many classics the quality is not good enough. If enough people ask for a title or a language, we will prioritize it.
faq.placeTitle: Why isn’t book X available where I live?
faq.place: Most often, from the country you are connecting from, that work is not yet free to use. Scrollia only publishes what is free worldwide: if the book is still under copyright in your country (or another), we do not offer it. It may also be that we have not onboarded it yet—in that case, write to us.
faq.pd: A work is in the public domain when copyright has expired (or never applied) and anyone may copy, translate, or share it without asking permission. The date is not the same in every country: it depends on local law (for example, years after the author’s death). That is why a book can be free in one place and still protected in another.
faq.sourceTitle: Where do the texts come from?
faq.source: From the Project Gutenberg corpus and, when a careful free edition exists, from Standard Ebooks and other open sources. At Scrollia we review, unify metadata, and translate when needed. Each work page cites its source; synopses often come from Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0).
faq.adsTitle: Why are there no ads or accounts?
faq.ads: Because literary heritage should not sit behind a paywall or a profile. Without accounts there is no cloud sync and no data to sell; without ads there is no incentive to track you. Your library, progress, and settings stay on your device. Server and editorial costs are borne by the project; if a support page appears someday, it will be voluntary and separate.
faq.typoTitle: How do I report a typo?
faq.typo: Email contact@scrollia.org with the title, language, and if you can, the chapter or a short quote. For now it is by email; later there will be an easier way from the reader itself.
